label: Supply edge: partial co-ground or sufficient supply
term: supply edge of the closed-collection Profile
resolution: The Profile edge m.grounds used by CCR (aca3baa1-9be6-4720-a53d-22050e638561), borrowed reality (45890c84-1d33-4273-b0ea-0f75bfd67a33), supplier concreteness and the ConcreteRootAccess batch is neutral: every registered theorem there holds whichever sense an edge takes, and no statement selects one. The localized bridge (a485166e-4868-4a0f-b017-ab095c16e202) demands root access for every concrete recipient with any actual nonconcrete supplier, whatever the sense. The two senses matter for the rival comparison only. The motivation 'harmless abstract co-grounds' reads an abstract edge as SUPPLY_EDGE_1: the abstract supplier does not select existence, but its edge stays in the selected relation, so supply-closure still counts it and borrowed reality holds vacuously on the mixed profile; treating the concrete network as a pure rootless network would need a different relation without that edge, which no record justifies. The mixed realization-law rival reads it as SUPPLY_EDGE_2: under CONCRETE_6 a nonconcrete sufficient supplier of esse owes an account of supplying esse without esse in re (docs/notes/esse-root-leaves.md, (f) row 6). No argument passes from one sense to the other. Both senses are modal-covariation proxies: they exclude each other constructively and, under explicit excluded middle, cover every actual edge (ConcreteRootAccess.partial_or_sufficient), but only by construction. The proxies mis-sort two cases: a sufficient supplier of a contingent effect (a free sustaining cause, a necessary agent with a contingent effect) falls under SUPPLY_EDGE_1, and a partial contributor to a recipient that exists wherever it does (every NECESSARY_2 recipient) falls under SUPPLY_EDGE_2. Neither label may therefore be used to classify such a case.
